title: S3 durability, availability, and consistency
hook: S3 promises 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability and strong read-after-write consistency for new objects — but versioning and replication still matter for operational recovery.

blocks.text: Amazon S3 replicates data across multiple facilities in a Region for durability. Availability SLA varies by storage class. Since December 2020, S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for PUTs of new objects and overwrite PUTs and DELETEs. Versioning keeps multiple versions of an object; delete markers hide current version without purging history.

blocks.text: Interviewers still cite outdated eventual consistency. Versioning protects against accidental delete and overwrite. Cross-Region Replication (CRR) is DR geography, not a substitute for versioning within Region.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: 11 nines durability in Region, strong consistency for new objects since 2020, versioning for ops recovery, CRR for geographic DR.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Enable versioning
items.body: Required for replication and accidental delete recovery.

items.body: New PUT immediately readable; LIST may paginate large buckets.

diagram.title: Versioning and replication
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  PUT[PutObject v1] --> B[Bucket source]
  B --> V[Version 1 stored]
  PUT2[PutObject v2] --> V2[Version 2 current]
  B --> CRR[Cross-Region Replication]
  CRR --> DR[Bucket destination Region B]

snippet.label: Enable bucket versioning
snippet.code:
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning \
  --bucket my-app-data \
  --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket my-app-data
snippet.explanation: Once enabled, only suspended — not fully disabled without deleting versions.

snippet.label: List object versions
snippet.explanation: Shows version IDs and delete markers for recovery.

snippet.label: CRR rule in CloudFormation
snippet.code:
ReplicationConfiguration:
  Role: !GetAtt ReplicationRole.Arn
  Rules:
    - Id: ReplicateAll
      Status: Enabled
      Priority: 1
      Filter: {}
      DeleteMarkerReplication:
        Status: Enabled
      Destination:
        Bucket: !Sub arn:aws:s3:::${DestBucket}
        StorageClass: STANDARD
snippet.explanation: Requires versioning on source and destination. Replication is asynchronous.

snippet.label: Restore previous version
snippet.explanation: Copy old version over current to restore without deleting history.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Assuming delete removes data when versioning enabled — only adds delete marker. CRR without versioning on source fails. Expecting instant cross-Region read after write in source Region.

blocks.text: S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) SLA for predictable CRR lag. Object Lock WORM for compliance immutability. How to prove it in production: S3 Inventory version counts, replication metrics ReplicationLatency, and restore drill from delete marker.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying S3 is eventually consistent in 2026 gets rejected. Strong answer: strong for new PUTs since Dec 2020; versioning; CRR async.

interviewTakeaways: 11 nines durability — AWS manages within Region.
Strong read-after-write for new object PUTs since December 2020.
Versioning enables undelete; delete marker hides current version.
60s: Strong consistency new objects. Versioning for ops recovery. CRR async DR. Not backup alone.
Follow-up: difference delete marker and permanent delete?
commonPitfalls: Outdated eventual consistency answer — rejected in modern interviews.
Strong answer: strong since 2020; LIST still paginate carefully at scale.
CRR without versioning enabled on source bucket.
No lifecycle on noncurrent versions — unbounded storage cost.
